arxiv-2008-01315.title: Eikonal solutions for moment hierarchies of Chemical Reaction Networks in the limits of large particle number
arxiv-2008-01315.creator: Eric Smith, Supriya Krishnamurthy
arxiv-2008-01315.description: Abstract Trajectory-based methods are well-developed to approximate steady-state probability distributions for stochastic processes in large-system limits. The trajectories are solutions to equations of motion of Hamiltonian dynamical systems, and are known as eikonals. They also express the leading flow lines along which probability currents balance.

arxiv-2110-14236.title: Electron Preacceleration at Weak Quasi-perpendicular Intracluster Shocks: Effects of Preexisting Nonthermal Electrons Journal: The Astrophysical Journal
arxiv-2110-14236.creator: Ji-Hoon Ha, Dongsu Ryu, Hyesung Kang, Sunjung Kim
arxiv-2110-14236.description: Abstract Radio relics in the outskirts of galaxy clusters imply the diffusive shock acceleration (DSA) of electrons at merger-driven shocks with Mach number M s ≲ 3 − 4 M_{s}\lesssim 3-4 in the intracluster medium (ICM). Recent studies have suggested that electron preacceleration and injection, prerequisite steps for DSA, could occur at supercritical shocks with M s ≳ 2.

arxiv-2206-08200.title: Adiabatic regularization and preferred vacuum state for the λ ​ ϕ 4 \lambda\phi^{4} field theory in cosmological spacetimes
arxiv-2206-08200.creator: Antonio Ferreiro, Silvia Pla
arxiv-2206-08200.description: Abstract We extend the method of adiabatic regularization by introducing an arbitrary parameter μ \mu for an scalar field with quartic self-coupling in a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) spacetime at one-loop order. The subtraction terms constructed from this extended version allow us to define a preferred vacuum state at a fixed time η = η 0 \eta=\eta_{0} for this theory.

arxiv-2207-04146.title: Information Rates with Non Ideal Photon Detectors in Time-Entanglement Based QKD
arxiv-2207-04146.creator: Dunbar Birnie IV, Christopher Cheng, and Emina Soljanin
arxiv-2207-04146.description: Abstract We develop new methods of quantifying the impact of photon detector imperfections on achievable secret key rates in Time-Entanglement based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). We address photon detection timing jitter, detector downtime, and photon dark counts and show how each may decrease the maximum achievable secret key rate in different ways.

arxiv-2208-02820.title: MOVE: Effective and Harmless Ownership Verification via Embedded External Features
arxiv-2208-02820.creator: Yiming Li, Linghui Zhu, Xiaojun Jia, Yang Bai, Yong Jiang, Shu-Tao Xia, Xiaochun Cao, Kui Ren
arxiv-2208-02820.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yiming Li, Linghui Zhu, Xiaojun Jia, Yang Bai, Yong Jiang, Shu-Tao Xia, Xiaochun Cao, Kui Ren. Currently, deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely adopted in different applications. Despite its commercial values, training a well-performing DNN is resource-consuming. Accordingly, the well-trained model is valuable intellectual property for its owner. However, recent studies revealed the threats of model stealing, where the adversaries can obtain a function-similar copy of the victim model, even when they can only query the model.

arxiv-2404-17396.title: Onset of global instability in a premixed annular V-flame
arxiv-2404-17396.creator: Chuhan Wang 1,2, Christopher M. Douglas 2,3, Yu Guan 4, Chunxiao Xu 1 and Lutz Lesshafft 2
arxiv-2404-17396.description: Abstract We investigate self-excited axisymmetric oscillations of a lean premixed methane–air V-flame in a laminar annular jet. The flame is anchored near the rim of the centrebody, forming an inverted cone, while the strongest vorticity is concentrated along the outer shear layer of the annular jet.

arxiv-2502-09583.title: Learning to Coordinate with Experts
arxiv-2502-09583.creator: Mohamad H. Danesh, Tu Trinh, Benjamin Plaut, Nguyen X. Khanh
arxiv-2502-09583.description: Abstract When deployed in dynamic environments, AI agents will inevitably encounter challenges that exceed their individual capabilities. Leveraging assistance from expert agents—whether human or AI—can significantly enhance safety and performance in such situations. However, querying experts is often costly, necessitating the development of agents that can efficiently request and utilize expert guidance.
